readings.title: The Earth Emptied and Plundered
readings.subtitle: Judgment Falls on All Alike
readings.text:
[Isaiah 24:1] See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is making the earth empty and making it waste, and shall overturn <dn>את</dn> its surface, and shall scatter abroad its inhabitants.
[2] And it shall be – as with the people so with the priest, as with the servant so with his master, as with the female servant so with her mistress, as with the buyer so with the seller, as with the lender so with the borrower, as with the creditor so with the debtor;
[3] the earth is completely emptied and utterly plundered, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken this word.
[4] The earth shall mourn and wither, the world shall languish and wither, the haughty people of the earth shall languish.
[5] For the earth has been defiled under its inhabitants, because they have transgressed <dn>את</dn> the Torot, changed the law, broken <dn>את</dn> the everlasting covenant.
[6] Therefore a curse shall consume <dn>את</dn> the earth, and those who dwell in it be punished. Therefore the inhabitants of the earth shall be burned, and few men shall be left.
[7] The new wine shall fail, the vine shall languish, all those glad at heart shall sigh.
[8] The joy of the tambourine shall cease, the noise of those who rejoice shall end, the joy of the lyre shall cease.
[9] No more do they drink wine with a song, strong drink is bitter to those who drink it.
[10] The deserted city shall be broken down, every house shall be shut, no one enters.
[11] There is a crying for wine in the streets; all joy shall be darkened, the gladness of the earth shall be gone.
[12] The city is left in ruins, and the gate is stricken with destruction.
[13] For thus it is to be in the midst of the earth among the peoples, like the shaking of an olive tree, like the gleaning of grapes when the grape harvest is done.

readings.title: A Remnant's Praise Amidst Chaos
readings.subtitle: The Day of YeHoVaH's Reign
readings.text:
[Isaiah 24:14] They lift up their voice, they sing of the excellency of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, they shall cry aloud from the sea.
[15] Therefore praise <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the east, the Name of <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl in the coastlands of the sea.
[16] From the ends of the earth we shall hear songs, “Splendour to the Righteous One!” But <dn>I</dn> say, “<dn>I</dn> waste away, <dn>I</dn> waste away! Woe to me! The treacherous betray, with treachery the treacherous betray.”
[17] Fear and the pit and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth.
[18] And it shall be that he who flees from the noise of the fear falls into the pit, and he who comes up from the midst of the pit is caught in the snare. For the windows from on high shall be opened, and the foundations of the earth be shaken.
[19] The earth shall be utterly broken, the earth shall be completely shattered, the earth shall be fiercely shaken.
[20] The earth shall stagger like a drunkard. And it shall totter like a hut, and its transgression shall be heavy upon it, and it shall fall, and not rise again.
[21] And in that day it shall be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> punishes on high <dn>את</dn> the host of exalted ones, and on the earth <dn>את</dn> the sovereigns of the earth.
[22] And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and be punished after many days.
[23] And the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be ashamed, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts shall reign on Mount Tsiyon, and in Yerushalayim, and before <dn>His</dn> elders, in esteem!

readings.title: A Song of Exaltation
readings.subtitle: Praise for Judgment and Refuge
readings.text:
[Isaiah 25:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are my <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> exalt <dn>את</dn> <dn>You</dn>, <dn>I</dn> praise <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Name, for <dn>You</dn> shall do a wonder – counsels of long ago, trustworthiness, truth.
[2] For <dn>You</dn> shall make a city a heap, a walled city a ruin, a palace of foreigners to be a city no more – never to be rebuilt.
[3] Therefore a strong people praise <dn>You</dn>, the city of the ruthless nations fear <dn>You</dn>.
[4] For <dn>You</dn> shall be a refuge to the poor, a refuge to the needy in his distress, a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat. For the spirit of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall.
[5] <dn>You</dn> subdue <dn>את</dn> the noise of foreigners, as heat in a dry place; as heat in the shadow of a cloud, the singing of the ruthless is subdued.

readings.title: The Messianic Banquet
readings.subtitle: Death Swallowed Up Forever
readings.text:
[Isaiah 25:6] And in this mountain <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts shall make for all people a feast of choice pieces, a feast of old wines, of choice pieces with marrow, of old wines, well-refined.
[7] And <dn>He</dn> shall swallow up on this mountain <dn>את</dn> the surface of the covering which covers all people, and the veil which is spread over all nations.
[8] <dn>He</dn> shall swallow up <dn>את</dn> death forever, and the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall wipe away <dn>את</dn> tears from all faces, and take away <dn>את</dn> the reproach of <dn>His</dn> people from all the earth. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.
[9] And it shall be said in that day, “See, this is our <dn>Elohim</dn>. We have waited for <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> saves us. This is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, we have waited for <dn>Him</dn>, let us be glad and rejoice in <dn>His</dn> deliverance.”
[10] For the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rests on this mountain, and Mo’aḇ is trodden down under <dn>Him</dn>, as straw is trodden down in the water of a dunghill.
[11] And <dn>He</dn> shall spread out <dn>His</dn> hands in their midst as he who swims spreads out his hands to swim, and <dn>He</dn> shall bring down their pride together, with the skill of <dn>His</dn> hands.
[12] And the high stronghold of <dn>את</dn> your walls <dn>He</dn> shall bring down, lay it low, levelled to the ground, down to the dust.

readings.title: The Strong City of Deliverance
readings.subtitle: Trust in the Rock of Ages
readings.text:
[Isaiah 26:1] In that day this song is sung in the land of Yehuḏah, <dq>“We have a strong city – <dn>He</dn> sets up deliverance, walls and ramparts.</dq>
[2] <dq>“Open the gates, let the righteous nation which guards the truth enter in.</dq>
[3] <dq>“The one steadfast of mind <dn>You</dn> guard in perfect peace, for he trusts in <dn>You</dn>.</dq>
[4] <dq>“Trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forever, for in Yah, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, is a rock of ages.</dq>
[5] <dq>“For <dn>He</dn> shall bring down those who dwell on high. <dn>He</dn> lays the exalted city low, <dn>He</dn> lays it low to the earth, <dn>He</dn> brings it down to the dust.</dq>
[6] <dq>“A foot tramples it down – feet of the poor, footsteps of the needy.”</dq>

readings.title: The Path of the Righteous
readings.subtitle: A Prayer for Deliverance and Resurrection
readings.text:
[Isaiah 26:7] The path of the righteous is uprightness; O upright One, <dn>You</dn> weigh <dn>את</dn> the course of the righteous.
[8] Also, in the path of <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, we have waited for <dn>You</dn>; the longing of our being is for <dn>Your</dn> Name and for the remembrance of <dn>You</dn>.
[9] <dn>My</dn> being longs for <dn>You</dn> in the night, also, my spirit within me seeks <dn>You</dn> earnestly. For when <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn righteousness.
[10] The wrong finds favour, yet he shall not learn righteousness; in the land of straightforwardness he acts perversely, and does not see the excellency of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[11] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>Your</dn> hand is high, they do not see. They see the ardour of the people and are ashamed; also, let the fire for <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> adversaries consume them.
[12] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> establish peace for us, for <dn>You</dn> have also done all our works in us.
[13] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, other masters besides <dn>You</dn> have had rule over us; only in <dn>You</dn> do we make mention of <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Name.
[14] The dead do not live; the departed spirits do not rise. Therefore <dn>You</dn> have visited and destroyed them, and made all <dn>את</dn> their remembrance to perish.
[15] <dn>You</dn> shall increase <dn>את</dn> the nation, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> shall increase <dn>את</dn> the nation; <dn>You</dn> are esteemed; <dn>You</dn> shall expand all <dn>את</dn> the borders of the land.
[16] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in distress they shall visit <dn>You</dn>, they shall pour out a prayer when <dn>Your</dn> disciplining is upon them.
[17] As a woman with child and about to give birth writhes and cries out in her pain, so shall we be before <dn>Your</dn> face, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[18] We have conceived, we writhed in pain; we have given birth to wind. We have not accomplished deliverance in the earth, nor have the inhabitants of the world fallen.
[19] Let <dn>Your</dn> dead live, together with my dead body, let them arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in dust; for <dn>Your</dn> dew is a dew of light, and let the earth give birth to <dn>את</dn> the departed spirits.

readings.title: Hide Until the Wrath is Past
readings.subtitle: The Punishment of Leviathan
readings.text:
[Isaiah 26:20] <dq>Go, <dn>my</dn> people, enter <dn>your</dn> rooms, and shut <dn>your</dn> doors behind <dn>you</dn>; hide <dn>yourself</dn>, as it were, for a little while, until the displeasure is past.</dq>
[21] For look, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is coming out of <dn>His</dn> place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their crookedness. And the earth shall disclose her blood, and no longer cover her killed ones.
[Isaiah 27:1] In that day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with <dn>His</dn> severe sword, great and strong, punishes <dn>את</dn> Liviathan the fleeing serpent, <dn>את</dn> Liviathan that twisted serpent. And <dn>He</dn> shall kill <dn>את</dn> the monster that is in the sea.

readings.title: The Vineyard of Red Wine
readings.subtitle: The Regathering of Israel
readings.text:
[Isaiah 27:2] In that day sing to her, <dq>“A vineyard of red wine!</dq>
[3] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do guard it, <dn>I</dn> water it every moment; lest any hurt it, <dn>I</dn> guard it night and day.</dq>
[4] <dq>“Wrath is not in <dn>Me</dn>. Who would set thornbushes and weeds against <dn>Me</dn> in battle? <dn>I</dn> would go through them, <dn>I</dn> would burn them together.</dq>
[5] <dq>“Or let him take hold of <dn>My</dn> strength and make peace with <dn>Me</dn>. Let him make peace with <dn>Me</dn>!”</dq>
[6] Those who come <dn>He</dn> causes to take root in Ya‛aqoḇ, Yisra’ěl shall blossom and bud. And they shall fill the face of the world with fruit.
[7] Has <dn>He</dn> smitten him as he struck <dn>את</dn> the ones who were striking him? Or as a killer – was he killed as he was killing?
[8] In measure, by sending her away, <dn>You</dn> contended with her. <dn>He</dn> shall take away by <dn>His</dn> rough wind in the day of the east wind.
[9] Therefore by this the crookedness of Ya‛aqoḇ is covered. And this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: when he makes all the stones of the slaughter-place like chalkstones that are beaten to dust – Ashěrim and sun-pillars rise no more.
[10] For the city of defence is lonely, a home forsaken and left like a wilderness – there the calf feeds, and there it lies down, and shall consume its branches.
[11] When its twigs are dry, they are broken off, women come and set them on fire. For it is a people of no understanding, therefore <dn>He</dn> who made them has no compassion on them, and <dn>He</dn> who formed them shows them no favour.
[12] And in that day it shall be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> threshes, from the channel of the River to the wadi of Mitsrayim. And you shall be gathered one by one, O children of Yisra’ěl.
[13] And in that day it shall be that a great shophar is blown, and those who were perishing in the land of Ashshur and the outcasts in the land of Mitsrayim shall come, and shall worship <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the set-apart mountain, in Yerushalayim.

readings.title: Woe to Ari'ěl
readings.subtitle: The Siege and Sudden Deliverance of Jerusalem
readings.text:
[Isaiah 29:1] Woe to Ari’ěl, to Ari’ěl, the city where Daviḏ dwelt! Add year to year, let festivals come around.
[2] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall distress <dn>את</dn> Ari’ěl, and there shall be mourning and sorrow, and it shall be to <dn>Me</dn> as Ari’ěl.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall encamp against <dn>you</dn> all around, <dn>I</dn> shall lay siege against <dn>you</dn> with a mound, and <dn>I</dn> shall raise siege-works against <dn>you</dn>.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And <dn>you</dn> shall be brought low and speak out of the ground, and <dn>your</dn> speech shall be low, out of the dust. And <dn>your</dn> voice shall be like a medium’s, out of the ground, and <dn>your</dn> speech whisper out of the dust.</dq>
[5] <dq>“But the crowd of those strange to <dn>you</dn> shall be like fine dust, and the crowd of the ruthless ones as chaff blowing away. And it shall be in an instant, suddenly!”</dq>
[6] <dn>You</dn> shall be visited by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and storm, and flame of devouring fire.
[7] Then the crowd of all the nations who fight against Ari’ěl, even all who fight against her and her stronghold, and distress her, shall be as a dream of a night vision.
[8] And it shall be as when a hungry man dreams, and see, he eats; but he awakes, and his being is empty; or as when a thirsty man dreams, and see, he drinks; but he awakes, and see, he is faint, and his being is longing. Thus shall the crowd of all the nations be who fight against Mount Tsiyon.

readings.title: A Spirit of Deep Sleep
readings.subtitle: Lip Service and Hidden Counsel
readings.text:
[Isaiah 29:9] Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
[10] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has poured out on you <dn>את</dn> the spirit of deep sleep, and has closed <dn>את</dn> your eyes, <dn>את</dn> the prophets. And <dn>He</dn> has covered <dn>את</dn> your heads, <dn>את</dn> the seers.
[11] And the entire vision is to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men give to one who knows books, saying, “Read this, please.” And he said, “<dn>I</dn> am unable, for it is sealed.”
[12] And the book is given to one who does not know books, saying, “Read this, please.” And he said, “<dn>I</dn> have not known books.”
[13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says, <dq>“Because this people has drawn near with its mouth, and with its lips they have esteemed <dn>Me</dn>, and it has kept its heart far from <dn>Me</dn>, and their fear of <dn>Me</dn> has become a command of men that is taught!</dq>
[14] <dq>“Therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am again doing a marvellous work among this people, a marvellous work and a wonder. And the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their clever men shall be hidden.”</dq>
[15] Woe to those who seek deep to hide their counsel far from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and their works are in the dark; they say, “Who sees us?” and, “Who knows us?”
[16] How perverse of you! Should the potter be reckoned as the clay? Should what is made say of its Maker, “<dn>He</dn> did not make me”? And what is formed say of <dn>Him</dn> who formed it, “<dn>He</dn> did not understand”?

readings.title: A Day of Restoration
readings.subtitle: The Deaf Shall Hear and the Blind Shall See
readings.text:
[Isaiah 29:17] Is it not yet a little while, and Leḇanon shall be turned into garden land, and garden land be reckoned as a forest?
[18] And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of gloom, and out of darkness.
[19] And the meek ones shall increase their joy in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the poor among men rejoice in the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl.
[20] For the ruthless one is brought to naught, the scorner is consumed, and all who watch for evil shall be cut off,
[21] those who make <dn>את</dn> a man to sin in word, and lay a snare for him who reproves in the gate, and turn aside <dn>את</dn> the righteous with empty reasoning.
[22] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who ransomed Aḇraham, concerning the house of Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“Ya‛aqoḇ is no longer put to shame, no longer does his face grow pale.</dq>
[23] <dq>“For when he sees his children, the work of <dn>My</dn> hands, in his midst, they shall set apart <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name, and set apart <dn>את</dn> the Set-apart One of Ya‛aqoḇ, and fear the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.</dq>
[24] <dq>“And those who went astray in spirit shall come to understanding, and the grumblers accept instruction.”</dq>
